posts.name: Rajagopalan Vaidyanathan
posts.cooked:
Hi,

In the end-term exam, the following question shows 3 options as valid options but the 2nd one sed 11p file.txt prints first 11 lines, not first 10 lines; how can it be correct?

This question can be interpreted as wanting to print only the 1st 10 lines (in which case this option is incorrect) or wanting to print the 1st 10 lines for sure but maybe more too (in which case this option is correct). Is my interpretation wrong if I go with the 1st one(first 10 lines only) ? Because the other two options only prints the 1st 10 lines and it is logical to expect the other options too to print the same number of lines.

I’ve tested this and have attached the results too where Option 1 and 3 prints only 1st 10 lines while option 2 prints 11 lines.

It’s unfair to play with words like this if my interpretation is wrong! We are not testing our English proficiency here!

Regards

Rajagopalan Vaidyanathan

This had happened with me during the 1st term exam.

The wording “the group can read” in English does not strictly exclude other permissions. It could be read as “the group can read (and possibly more),” whereas the expected answer assumes “the group can only read.”

While I understand now that I should have applied the principle of least privilege, I still feel that the phrasing of the question could have been clearer

posts.name: Rajagopalan Vaidyanathan
posts.cooked:
Since it’s said that “only” the owner can read and write, you’re right to assume that the group can read(and possibly execute too) but that is also incorrect(1st option). If they want the group to be able to “only” read then they should have explicitly mentioned that as they’ve said for owner.

This is exactly what I mean too - you cannot play with words knowingly or unknowingly - and is always better to give examples to explain what you mean. English is not our first language but the language we use for communication and English language as a subject is already done with in foundations.
